title: Why I'm Betting on AI Agents
subtitle: Or: How I Learned to Stop Micromanaging and Love Emergence

slots.anchor: A slightly ridiculous thought experiment helped me see the distinction.
slots.brief: Margin vignette: a small alien planet in cross-section with a primordial soup pool; floating above it, three offered seeds — a DNA helix, a small worn robot with a backpack, and a scroll titled by its shape alone as a requirements document (no readable text). Ink and watercolor, dry humor.

slots.anchor: ## When Search Moved Up a Level
slots.brief: Corner scene: an old wooden Go board mid-game seen over the shoulder of a human player; one stone glows faintly out of place, and a small hand-built robot on the far side leans in, having just played it. Spectators' teacups gone cold.

slots.text: Control doesn't disappear. It moves upward.

slots.anchor: The primordial soup isn't chemicals anymore.
slots.brief: Small spot: a laboratory flask whose liquid is made of tiny drifting tools and fragments — brackets, gears, a tiny compiler crank, punch-card plankton. One bubble rising. Cream background, soft edges, no readable text.
Margin vignette: a single stem bearing one beautiful flower and, lower, one unmistakable parasite vine gripping it — drawn with equal botanical care. Field-notebook style, quietly unsettling.

slots.anchor: ## Why I'm Still Betting on This
slots.text: Emergence can give us capable systems. It doesn't give us trustworthy systems.

slots.anchor: Cultivation may be a better metaphor
slots.brief: Small vignette: a gardener kneeling beside a young plant, hands open, deliberately not pulling; a discarded marionette cross-bar with slack strings lies in the grass behind them.
